status: Drafted by direct read-through of the real Ethiopian-translation verse text (Assets/Resources/Verses/Ethiopian/1_kings_11.json, all 22 chapters), cross-referenced against the existing KJV 1 Kings Character Index for structural/style consistency. Single-pass draft grounded in the actual extracted text, not yet run through a separate adversarial fact-check pass.
notes: This Ethiopian-translation text of 1 Kings is, chapter-for-chapter and verse-for-verse, the same narrative content as the standard KJV 1 Kings — 22 chapters, the same 816-verse count, same episodes in the same order (David's succession crisis, Solomon's reign/Temple/wisdom/apostasy, the kingdom's split under Rehoboam/Jeroboam, the northern dynasties Baasha-Zimri-Omri-Ahab, and the Elijah cycle through Ahab/Jehoshaphat). Unlike the Ethiopian Bible's own "Ezra" (a genuinely different 9-chapter 1-Esdras-tradition text), NO real structural or content divergence from the familiar canonical 1 Kings was found here after reading the full extracted text start to finish — this book did not need the kind of "don't force-fit KJV's structure" correction that book required. The tier/character structure below was authored independently against this translation's own text (not copy-pasted from the KJV Character Index), but naturally mirrors it closely given the identical underlying content; all character ids are suffixed _eth1kgs to avoid collision with the existing KJV CharacterIndex/1Kings.json ids. Naming collisions flagged, none silently merged: two men named Hiram (the king of Tyre, chs. 5/9, vs. the Naphtali-born bronze craftsman of ch. 7 — the text gives the craftsman no compound name); two men named Ben-hadad, treated as dynastically related but distinct individuals per the text's own "cities my father took from thy father" wording in 20:34 (Ben-hadad I under Asa in ch. 15, and Ben-hadad II who besieges Samaria and fights at Ramoth-gilead in chs. 20/22); Ahijah the Shilonite the prophet vs. Baasha's father, also named Ahijah (15:27) — unrelated men; Jehu the son of Hanani, a prophet condemning Baasha in ch. 16, flagged as distinct from the not-yet-acting Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom Elijah is told in 19:16 to anoint king (that Jehu's own reign is a later book, not indexed here). Solomon's twelve district officers and household officials (ch. 4) and the prophets of Baal/the groves (ch. 18) and Ahab's four hundred court prophets (ch. 22) are deliberately kept as collective genealogyLists entries rather than individualized — the text lists names/roles administratively without differentiating personal action, per the collective-entry rule. The widow of Zarephath's son (ch. 17) is given his own submanager entry despite being unnamed, since his death and resurrection is a full personally-embodied scene, not incidental — same test used for Genubath/Tahpenes in the existing KJV file.

characters.name: David

verses.note: Old and stricken in years; 'they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.'
Swears to Bathsheba, before witnesses, that Solomon will reign after him.
His final charge to Solomon: keep the LORD's statutes, deal with Joab and Shimei, show kindness to Barzillai's sons.
Dies and is buried in the city of David, having reigned 40 years — 7 in Hebron, 33 in Jerusalem.

funFacts: Abishag the Shunammite is brought to warm him in old age, though 'the king knew her not' (1:4).

characters.name: Bathsheba

verses.note: Goes in to David on Nathan's plan, reminding him of his oath that Solomon would reign.
Solomon rises, bows to her, and sets a throne for her at his right hand as 'the king's mother.'

funFacts: Later unwittingly relays Adonijah's fatal request for Abishag to Solomon (2:13-21).

verses.note: Instructs Bathsheba to go to David about Adonijah's self-proclaimed kingship.
Confirms Bathsheba's report and questions whether David himself ordered Adonijah's feast.

characters.name: Zadok the priest

verses.note: Anoints Solomon with the horn of oil out of the tabernacle at Gihon.
Put in the room of Abiathar as priest, once Solomon secures the throne.

funFacts: Sides with Solomon while Abiathar the priest sides with Adonijah — the priesthood itself splits over the succession (1:7-8).

characters.name: Adonijah

verses.note: 'Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king' — the text notes David 'had not displeased him at any time.'
Holds a sacrificial feast at the stone of Zoheleth by En-rogel, inviting his brothers and Judah's men, but not Solomon, Nathan, Benaiah, or the mighty men.
Solomon reads his request to marry Abishag as a renewed claim on the throne and has Benaiah execute him.

funFacts: His mother Haggith bore him 'after Absalom' per 1:6 — placing him next in birth order among David's surviving sons.

verses.note: Follows Adonijah, alongside Abiathar the priest.
David's dying charge names Joab's killing of Abner and Amasa 'in peace' as unfinished blood-guilt.
Flees to the tabernacle and grasps the altar's horns for sanctuary; Solomon has Benaiah kill him there anyway.
Follows Adonijah.

Banished to Anathoth and stripped of the priesthood rather than executed, since he 'barest the ark of the Lord GOD before David' — the text notes this fulfills an earlier word against the house of Eli.
Sought throughout Israel as 'a fair damsel' to cherish the aged David; the text states he 'knew her not.'
Adonijah asks Bathsheba to request her hand from Solomon — the request that gets him killed.

characters.name: Solomon

spouses: 700 wives and 300 concubines, per 11:3, not individually named
children: Taphath (wife of the son of Abinadab, 4:11)

verses.note: Asks God for 'an understanding heart to judge thy people' rather than riches or long life.
Judges between the two harlots over the living child, ordering the child divided — the episode that fixes his reputation for wisdom.
Begins building the house of the LORD in the 480th year after the Exodus, his 4th regnal year.
His many foreign wives 'turned away his heart after other gods'; builds high places for Chemosh and Molech.
Reigns 40 years over Israel; dies and is succeeded by Rehoboam.

funFacts: Spake 3,000 proverbs and 1,005 songs, and discoursed on trees from the cedar to the hyssop, and on beasts, fowl, creeping things, and fishes (4:32-33).
Received 666 talents of gold in one year alone, beside merchant and tribute income (10:14-15).

characters.name: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada

verses.note: Supports Solomon's anointing, escorting him to Gihon.
Kills Joab at Solomon's order and is made captain of the host in his place.
Listed among Solomon's chief officers, over the host.

funFacts: Personally executes Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei son of Gera on Solomon's orders (2:25, 2:34, 2:46).

characters.name: Shimei the son of Gera

verses.note: Solomon confines him to Jerusalem on pain of death.
Executed by Benaiah three years later for crossing the brook Kidron to Gath to retrieve runaway servants.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED: a different Benjamite Shimei (son of Elah, one of Solomon's twelve district officers, 4:18) is a separate man from this Shimei son of Gera.

characters.name: Hiram, king of Tyre

verses.note: Supplies cedar and fir timber for the Temple in exchange for wheat and oil; the two kings make a league, having been 'ever a lover of David.'
Given twenty cities in Galilee by Solomon, finds them displeasing, and names the land Cabul.
Sends his own seafaring servants alongside Solomon's in a joint navy to Ophir, returning 420 talents of gold.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED: distinct from Hiram the bronze craftsman of chapter 7 — same name, different man, different role.

characters.name: Hiram (the craftsman)

genealogy.father: a man of Tyre, a worker in brass (unnamed)

verses.note: Fetched from Tyre; 'a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali,' filled with wisdom and cunning to work all works in brass.
Casts the two bronze pillars, named Jachin and Boaz, for the temple porch.
Casts the molten sea — a round bronze basin ten cubits across, resting on twelve oxen.
Finishes all the bronze vessels for the house of the LORD.

funFacts: The text gives him no compound name — just 'Hiram,' explicitly distinct from the king of Tyre who sent for him.

characters.name: The Temple Dedication and the LORD's Covenant Response
characters.purpose: Establishes that the newly built Temple's holiness and the LORD's presence there are conditioned on covenant obedience, not automatic — Solomon's own dedication prayer anticipates Israel's future sin, defeat, famine, and exile, and the LORD's night-vision response warns that turning to other gods will get Israel 'cut off' and the house made 'a proverb and a byword' among the nations. It frames the rest of the book's descent into division and idolatry as already foretold at the height of Solomon's own glory.

verses.note: The cloud fills the house of the LORD at its dedication so that the priests cannot stand to minister.
Solomon's dedication prayer, spread-handed toward heaven, including petitions for Israel in defeat, famine, and captivity.
The LORD's response in a second night appearance: hallows the house, but warns that apostasy will cut Israel off and cast the house from His sight.

characters.name: The Queen of Sheba

verses.note: Comes 'to prove him with hard questions'; Solomon answers all of them, 'there was not any thing hid from the king.'
Declares 'the half was not told me' after seeing his wisdom, house, table, and ascent to the LORD's house.
Gives Solomon 120 talents of gold and the greatest abundance of spices Israel ever received.
Solomon gives her all her desire 'of his royal bounty'; she returns to her own country.

funFacts: No personal name is given — 'Sheba' names her kingdom, not a father; the text asserts no later identification for her.

characters.name: Hadad the Edomite

spouses: the sister of Tahpenes the queen, unnamed

verses.note: 'Of the king's seed in Edom'; flees to Egypt as a small child when Joab's campaign kills every male in Edom.
Given the sister of queen Tahpenes to wife by Pharaoh's favor; she bears Genubath.
Asks Pharaoh's leave to return to Edom once he hears David and Joab are both dead.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED: distinct from an earlier Edomite king also named Hadad, and from the 'Ben-hadad' element used elsewhere for Syrian kings.

genealogy.mother: the sister of Tahpenes the queen, unnamed

verses.note: Born to Hadad and Tahpenes's sister; weaned by Tahpenes herself and raised in Pharaoh's own household 'among the sons of Pharaoh.'
Pharaoh gives Hadad her own sister in marriage, 'the sister of Tahpenes the queen.'
Personally weans Genubath, Hadad's son, in Pharaoh's house.

characters.name: Rezon the son of Eliadah

verses.note: Flees from his former lord Hadadezer king of Zobah, gathers a band of men, and seizes Damascus.
'An adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon...reigned over Syria.'

funFacts: His Hadadezer of Zobah is a separate figure from Hadad the Edomite despite the similar name.

characters.name: Rehoboam

verses.note: Israel asks him to lighten the heavy yoke Solomon laid on them.
Rejects the elders' counsel, following the young men instead: 'my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.'
Ten tribes revolt, crying 'To your tents, O Israel' — the kingdom splits, save the tribe of Judah.
Shishak king of Egypt invades in his 5th year and empties the treasures of the Temple and king's house.

funFacts: Reigned 17 years in Jerusalem before his death (14:21, 14:31).

verses.note: Delivers the LORD's word forbidding Rehoboam's assembled 180,000 warriors from fighting Israel: 'this thing is from me' — the army stands down.
Solomon's own servant, 'a mighty man of valour,' made ruler over the labor force of the house of Joseph before his rebellion.
Ahijah the Shilonite tears his own new garment into twelve pieces and gives Jeroboam ten, prophesying his kingship over ten tribes.
Sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan specifically to keep the people from returning to worship at Jerusalem — a stated political calculation.
Reigns 22 years; dies and is succeeded by his son Nadab.

characters.name: Ahijah the Shilonite

verses.note: Tears his new garment into twelve pieces, gives Jeroboam ten, prophesying his kingship.
Though 'his eyes were set by reason of his age' (blind), recognizes Jeroboam's disguised wife by the sound of her feet at the door.
Prophesies the death of Jeroboam's son Abijah and the eventual cutting off of the whole house of Jeroboam.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED: a different man also named Ahijah is Baasha's father (15:27) — unrelated to this prophet.

verses.note: Disguises herself on Jeroboam's orders and travels to Shiloh to ask Ahijah what will become of their sick son.
The child dies the instant her foot crosses the threshold of their own house at Tirzah, exactly as foretold.

characters.name: Abijah, son of Jeroboam

verses.note: Falls sick, prompting his mother's disguised journey to Ahijah.
Dies as prophesied; alone of Jeroboam's whole house he is mourned and buried, since 'in him there is found some good thing toward the LORD.'

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED: not the same person as Abijam, king of Judah and Rehoboam's son — two different men in overlapping timeframes.

characters.name: The man of God out of Judah

verses.note: Cries against the altar at Bethel by the word of the LORD, giving the sign that it shall be rent and its ashes poured out.
Ahab's — actually Jeroboam's — hand withers when he orders him seized, then is restored at his prayer.
Given explicit command: eat no bread, drink no water, and return not by the way he came.
Deceived into disobeying, he is killed by a lion on the road; the lion strangely neither eats the body nor mauls the standing donkey.

funFacts: Names a future king, 'Josiah,' by name as the one who will one day burn idolatrous priests' bones on this very altar (13:2) — its fulfillment is recorded roughly 300 years later, in a later book not indexed here.

characters.name: The old prophet who dwelt in Bethel

children: unnamed sons who report the man of God's actions to him, 13:11

verses.note: Follows and deceives the man of God into eating bread at his house — the text states plainly 'he lied unto him.'
Recognizes the death as the LORD's fulfilled word, retrieves and buries the body, and instructs his own sons to lay his bones beside the man of God's when he dies.
Does right in the eyes of the LORD, removes the sodomites, and puts away the idols his fathers made.
Removes his own grandmother Maachah from the queen mother's position for making an idol; 'his heart was perfect with the LORD all his days,' though the high places remain.
Sends silver and gold from the Temple and his own house to Ben-hadad of Syria to break his league with Baasha.
In old age, 'diseased in his feet.'

characters.name: Maachah

verses.note: Named 'the daughter of Abishalom,' mother of Abijam.
Deposed by her own grandson Asa 'because she had made an idol in a grove'; the idol is burnt at the brook Kidron.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED: 'Maachah' recurs for other figures elsewhere in scripture; within 1 Kings the text calls her 'mother' of both Abijam and (later) Asa, functioning as an idiom for the continuing queen-mother office rather than a literal claim she birthed Asa himself.

characters.name: Ben-hadad (I), king of Syria, son of Tabrimon

verses.note: Accepts Asa's treasure, breaks his existing league with Baasha, and captures Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maachah, and all Naphtali.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED, MAJOR: a separate figure from the Ben-hadad of chapters 20/22 who besieges Samaria under Ahab — 20:34's 'cities my father took from thy father' implies dynastic succession between the two rather than identity, so they are kept as two distinct entries here.

characters.name: Baasha

verses.note: Conspires against Nadab while he besieges the Philistine city Gibbethon, kills him, and reigns in his stead.
Kills all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none remaining, fulfilling Ahijah's earlier word.
Dies and is succeeded by his son Elah.

funFacts: His father, also named Ahijah (15:27), is a different man from Ahijah the Shilonite the prophet.

verses.note: Reigns two years over Israel, 'walked in the way of his father,' and is killed by Baasha at Gibbethon.

characters.name: Jehu the son of Hanani

verses.note: The word of the LORD comes to him against Baasha, condemning him for walking in Jeroboam's way and for killing Jeroboam's house.
Reiterates the judgment against Baasha's dynasty.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED: distinct from Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom Elijah is told in 19:16 to anoint as future king of Israel — not yet acting in this book, and unrelated to this prophet.

verses.note: Kills Elah, 'captain of half his chariots,' while Elah was drinking himself drunk in Tirzah, and reigns in his stead.
Slays the entire house of Baasha the moment he sits on the throne, leaving 'not one that pisseth against a wall.'
Reigns only seven days before, besieged in Tirzah by Omri's forces, he burns the king's house down over himself.
Reigns two years; killed by his own officer Zimri while drunk in the house of Arza, steward of his house.

characters.name: Omri

verses.note: 'All Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp,' after Zimri's death was reported.
Israel splits between Tibni's faction and his own; Omri prevails, and Tibni dies.
Reigns 12 years total; buys the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and builds Israel's future capital there, naming it after him.

funFacts: The text's summary judgment on him is unusually brief and harsh: 'did worse than all that were before him' (16:25).

verses.note: Half of Israel follows him for king against Omri; the text states only that 'Tibni died' once Omri's faction prevails, giving no cause.

characters.name: Ahab

verses.note: 'Did evil in the sight of the LORD above all that were before him'; marries Jezebel, serves Baal, builds him a temple in Samaria.
Calls Elijah 'he that troubleth Israel'; Elijah answers that it is Ahab's own house that has forsaken the LORD's commandments.
Goes down to take possession of Naboth's vineyard once told Naboth is dead.
Rends his clothes, fasts, and lies in sackcloth on hearing Elijah's judgment; the LORD defers the disaster to his son's days because of this humbling.
A stray arrow finds him 'between the joints of the harness' at Ramoth-gilead; he dies propped in his chariot, and dogs lick his blood as the chariot is washed at Samaria.

funFacts: Reigned 22 years over Israel in Samaria (16:29).

verses.note: Reigns in his father Ahab's stead.
Reigns two years over Israel in Samaria; 'did evil...walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother' — his reign closes the book.

characters.name: Jezebel

verses.note: Taken to wife by Ahab; he then serves and worships Baal.
Cuts off the LORD's prophets, prompting Obadiah to hide a hundred of them by fifty in a cave, fed with bread and water.
Sends word to Elijah threatening his life 'by to morrow about this time,' driving him into the wilderness.
Writes letters in Ahab's name and seal to frame and stone Naboth so Ahab can seize his vineyard.
The LORD's specific judgment through Elijah: 'the dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'

funFacts: Feeds 450 prophets of Baal and 400 prophets of the groves 'at Jezebel's table' (18:19).

verses.note: Refuses to sell or trade his vineyard to Ahab: 'The LORD forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.'
Falsely accused of blasphemy by two suborned witnesses at Jezebel's direction, then stoned to death outside the city.

characters.name: Elijah the Tishbite

verses.note: Declares to Ahab there will be neither dew nor rain 'these years, but according to my word.'
Challenges the prophets of Baal at Carmel: the god who answers by fire shall be God.
Fire falls and consumes his sacrifice, wood, stones, dust, and the water in the trench; the people declare 'The LORD, he is the God,' and the prophets of Baal are slain at the brook Kishon.
At Horeb, the LORD is not in the wind, the earthquake, or the fire, but in 'a still small voice.'
Casts his mantle on Elisha the son of Shaphat, who is plowing with twelve yoke of oxen.
Meets Ahab in Naboth's vineyard and pronounces the LORD's judgment against his house.

funFacts: Fed by ravens at the brook Cherith, then sustained by a widow's never-emptying barrel of meal and cruse of oil at Zarephath (17:6, 17:14-16).

verses.note: 'Feared the LORD greatly'; hid a hundred of the LORD's prophets by fifty in a cave and fed them with bread and water when Jezebel was slaying them.
Meets Elijah on the road, fears reprisal from Ahab if Elijah vanishes again, but carries the message to Ahab anyway.
Gathering sticks at the city gate to prepare her and her son's last meal before, she expects, they starve.
Obeys Elijah's request to feed him first; her barrel of meal and cruse of oil do not fail for the rest of the famine.
Accuses Elijah, when her son dies, of coming 'to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son.'
Declares, once her son is revived, 'now by this I know that thou art a man of God.'

characters.name: The widow of Zarephath's son

verses.note: Falls sick 'so sore, that there was no breath left in him.'
Elijah stretches himself on him three times and cries to the LORD; 'the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.'

funFacts: Left unnamed by the text, but given his own entry here since his death and revival is a full, personally-embodied scene, not incidental to his mother's.

characters.name: Elisha the son of Shaphat

verses.note: The LORD instructs Elijah at Horeb to anoint him prophet in his own room.
Found plowing with twelve yoke of oxen; Elijah casts his mantle on him. He slaughters his own oxen for a farewell feast, then follows and ministers to Elijah.

funFacts: His own prophetic ministry (2 Kings) is not indexed here — only his call, within 1 Kings, is asserted.

characters.name: Ben-hadad (II), king of Syria

verses.note: Gathers thirty-two allied kings, besieges Samaria, and demands Ahab's silver, gold, wives, and children.
Drinking himself drunk in the pavilions with the kings when Israel's young men attack; the Syrians flee, and he escapes on horseback.
Sues for his life in sackcloth; Ahab spares him and makes a covenant, restoring cities and granting Israelite streets in Damascus.
His continued hold on Ramoth-gilead, 'ours' by Israel's own claim, sets up the war in which Ahab dies.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED, MAJOR: kept distinct from Ben-hadad I of Syria (ch. 15, under Asa) — see that entry's note.

characters.name: Jehoshaphat

verses.note: Agrees to join Ahab against Ramoth-gilead: 'I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses.'
Asks whether there is a prophet of the LORD besides the four hundred, leading to Micaiah being summoned.
Mistaken for the king of Israel in his royal robes and nearly killed in battle; the Syrian captains withdraw once they see he is not Ahab.
'Walked in all the ways of Asa his father...doing that which was right in the eyes of the LORD,' though the high places remained.
His Tarshish ships bound for Ophir's gold are wrecked at Ezion-geber; he refuses Ahaziah's offer to send servants on a second attempt.

funFacts: Reigned 25 years in Jerusalem (22:42).

verses.note: The king of Israel names him as 'one man' who could inquire of the LORD, adding 'I hate him; for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil.'
Tells the summoning messenger, 'As the LORD liveth, what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak.'
Recounts a vision of the LORD's throne room, where a spirit volunteers to be 'a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets' to persuade Ahab to his death.
Ordered imprisoned and fed the bread and water of affliction 'until I come in peace.'
'If thou return at all in peace, the LORD hath not spoken by me.'

characters.name: Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah

verses.note: Makes himself horns of iron and prophesies, 'With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until thou have consumed them.'
Strikes Micaiah on the cheek, demanding, 'Which way went the Spirit of the LORD from me to speak unto thee?'

funFacts: Leads the roughly four hundred court prophets who unanimously (and falsely) urge Ahab to battle.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

barzillais_sons.note: David charges Solomon to show kindness to 'the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite,' unnamed, for sheltering David from Absalom.

solomons_twelve_officers.note: Twelve named district officers (Ben-hur, Ben-dekar, Ben-hesed, Ben-abinadab, Baana, Ben-geber, Ahinadab, Ahimaaz, Baanah, Jehoshaphat, Shimei son of Elah, Geber son of Uri) who each provisioned the king's household one month a year — an administrative list, not individualized into scribe tiers/characters since the text differentiates only assignments, not personal actions.

solomons_household_officials.note: Azariah son of Zadok the priest; Elihoreph and Ahiah sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, recorder; Azariah son of Nathan, over the officers; Zabud son of Nathan, principal officer and the king's friend; Ahishar, over the household; Adoniram son of Abda, over the tribute. Kept as a bulk administrative list.

prophets_of_baal_and_the_groves.note: 450 prophets of Baal and 400 prophets of the groves who eat at Jezebel's table; the 450 of Baal are slain at Kishon after the fire-contest. Treated as a collective cultic body, not individualized.

ahabs_four_hundred_prophets.note: Roughly 400 court prophets who unanimously urge Ahab to battle at Ramoth-gilead; Zedekiah son of Chenaanah is drawn out individually (see his entry) but the rest remain a collective.

davids_seven_hundred_wives_and_solomons_.note: Solomon's 700 wives and 300 concubines are given only as a numeric total, no individual names beyond Pharaoh's daughter (own entry via Solomon) and Naamah the Ammonitess (Rehoboam's mother, 14:21).
